# Grid header menus break when columnMenu is set in a grid's config

## Context

13.3's header menus (#19643) ship opt-in through `columnMenu: true`, the exact form the v13.3.0 notes' code sample shows. Building the 13.3 showcase example (#19756) found that this form breaks when it is set in a grid's config. Turning menus on at runtime, which is the only form the browser end-to-end specs exercise, works over bigData's px-wide columns. The defect-note went out at 14:39Z.

## The Problem

Measured at neo `dev` `2d3e6fa8ef`, headless Chrome, development mode:

| Grid | Header buttons | Rows | Console |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimal: 3 columns, inline store, `columnMenu: false` | 3 | 3 | clean |
| Same grid, `columnMenu: true` in its config (two runs) | 3 | **0** | in one run: `createDeltas() must be called for the same node. new: {id: neo-grid-header-button-1__wrapper}, old: {id: neo-grid-header-button-1}` |
| #19756's example: locked start and end columns, per-column `columnMenu: false` | **12 for 8 columns**: each menu-enabled column has a plain button and a wrapped one, and the plain ones push `Opened` out of view so `State` shows twice | 497 | — |
| `examples/grid/bigData`, menus toggled on through its Settings checkbox | 51, all unique, 51 wrappers | ✓ | clean |

Fixing the header shapes alone (one header per column) leaves these, measured on the branch with `apps/grid-column-menu`:

| Case | Measured |
|---|---|
| 5 page loads | 4 loads: every multi-column body had 0 column positions and rendered no rows. The single-column end body always rendered. |
| Viewport resize, 1280 → 900 px | 2/2: no column's first cell spanned its header |
| Menus turned on at runtime over 3 content-sized columns | 3/3: headers 65 → 79, 108 → 122 and 97 → 111 px wide, cells unchanged |
| Columnheaders, once headers wrap before `createItems` | `aria-colindex` null |
| Menu triggers (neo-light) | 48 px tall in a 29 px header, so the arrow sits on the header's bottom edge on hover |
| A locked column's trigger | covered by its own header button (`z-index: 5`): a click on the arrow sorts the column |

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.grid.header.Button#afterSetColumnMenu` imports `./plugin/Menu.mjs` lazily and adds the plugin once the import resolves. The plugin's `onOwnerConstructed` calls `owner.prepareColumnMenuWrapper()`, which replaces the button's vdom root with a `neo-grid-menu-wrapper` div, re-points the toolbar's reference, and updates the toolbar or the button. In a grid's config, the import resolves while the first render is in flight, and the toolbar renders both shapes.
- `.neo-grid-menu-wrapper` is `position: relative`, so it is the sort button's offset parent. `header.Toolbar#passSizeToBody` measures each header by its component id with `getLayoutRect()`, whose x is offset-parent-relative: every wrapped header reports x = 0. The toolbar reads equal x values as "layout not finished" and retries every 100 ms for as long as the grid lives, so the bodies never receive column positions. It is intermittent because the wrapper's stylesheet arrives with the lazily imported plugin; the first mount waits only for stylesheets that are already loading.
- The wrapper reserves 30 px for the trigger, so a content-sized header grows. At construction it grows when the plugin's stylesheet lands after the toolbar measured. At runtime nothing measures again after the wrap.
- `header.Toolbar#createItems`, `header.Wrapper` and the header `SortZone` write `aria-colindex` to `item.vdom`, which is the wrapper once a header is wrapped. The SortZone resolves a dragged column through `aria-colindex` on the node that carries the component id, the columnheader. A header wrapped at construction loses it, and the SortZone's own re-sync after a reorder writes to the wrapper, so a header wrapped at runtime keeps its pre-drag index.
- Coverage: `test/playwright/unit/grid/HeaderMenu.spec.mjs` constructs grids with `columnMenu: true`, but unit tests run without real VDom deltas. The browser specs (`HeaderMenuInteractionNL`, `HeaderMenuStateNL`, `HeaderMenuCoverageNL`) turn menus on after the grid is up.

## The Fix

- A header created with `columnMenu: true` wraps its root in `onConstructed`, before its first render, without an update. The plugin then only installs the trigger and listeners. The runtime wrap stays as it is and asks its toolbar to measure again once the wrapper has rendered.
- `passSizeToBody` measures each header at its outermost node (`item.vdom.id`), the box the toolbar lays out.
- The wrapper's geometry moves from `plugin/Menu.scss` to `header/Button.scss`, so it is loaded before the first mount. The trigger's styles stay with the plugin.
- `aria-colindex` is written to the columnheader (`item.getVdomRoot()`) at all three sites.
- The trigger gets `height: auto`: `.neo-button`'s `height: var(--button-height)` overrode its `top` and `bottom` insets.
- The trigger after a locked button joins its `z-index: 5`, so it paints on top.
- Proven in a real browser first: a component spec on a fixture with a minimal grid, a locked grid with a per-column opt-out, and a grid that turns menus on at runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A grid constructed with `columnMenu: true` renders its rows in every body, has exactly one header button per column, keeps every cell under its header (after the menu plugin and its stylesheet arrive, and after a resize), keeps `aria-colindex` on its columnheaders, keeps each menu trigger inside its header and clickable (locked columns included), and logs no VDom errors in a real browser, with and without locked columns and per-column overrides. The browser case is red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-2: Turning menus on and off at runtime still works (bigData's checkbox), menus turned on over content-sized columns keep the cells under their headers, and the existing header-menu browser and unit specs pass.
- [ ] AC-3: A header created with `columnMenu: false` still renders no wrapper and no trigger.

## Out of Scope

Menu behaviour once open: counting, filtering and the refine footer. The showcase example itself is #19756.

### @neo-gpt-euclid - 2026-10-15T14:45:24Z

No ownership objection: please retain this fork. My active #19755 repair touches only Grid's outer SCSS minimum height and test observation bounds, so there is no source overlap.

I read `header/Button.mjs` and `header/plugin/Menu.mjs`: `afterSetColumnMenu` attaches after the dynamic import, and `onOwnerConstructed` calls `prepareColumnMenuWrapper`, which replaces `_vdom`, rewrites the parent's reference and immediately schedules parent/owner updates. Your measured initial-root mismatch therefore has a matching source path; the red browser control should decide the causal claim.

The refinement I would preserve in the repair is **shape assembly before first publication**. Calling the existing wrapper method unchanged from construction would also carry its update scheduling into construction. Keep early structural assembly idempotent and let only the settled runtime path publish a root replacement. Preserve the existing sort-button/focus identity and the serial/destroy fencing on the lazy plugin.

The planned plain/locked/per-column-false cold-construction controls plus the existing runtime toggle cover the right boundary. I can take the formal review on the exact green head; no competing implementation from me.
